audited_source_corrections.action: Require the eigenconstant to be absent from both the conclusion sequent and the existential major premise's end formula.
audited_source_corrections.source_issue_or_choice: The N2 caption repeats absence from the conclusion sequent but omits absence from the existential major premise formula. This permits an unsound application when A(x) contains the same constant a outside the replaced variable.
audited_source_corrections.chosen_treatment: The Tamil caption retains the conclusion-sequent condition and adds that, in existential elimination, a must also be absent from the major premise's end formula.
audited_source_corrections.alternatives_considered: Translate the repeated source condition literally, or silently alter a displayed rule instead of stating the missing side condition.
audited_source_corrections.rationale: With A(x)=R(x,a), Gamma_1 asserting forall y exists x R(x,y), and Gamma_2 asserting forall y not R(y,y), the printed restriction permits existential elimination to derive arbitrary C from a satisfiable two-element irreflexive serial relation. Excluding a from the major premise formula blocks this counterexample and matches the adjacent N1 and first-order quantifier explanations.
audited_source_corrections.precise_review_question: Does N2 existential elimination require a to be absent from the major premise formula as well as the conclusion sequent?
